evidence_quotes: A total of 79 significant earthquakes (M4.5 or greater) rattled the globe over the past 30 days
Tobelo, Indonesia led all hotspots with 11 recorded events
Nikolski, Alaska ranked second with 9 events
February 3 was the busiest single day, logging 7 earthquakes
ranging from shallow (1.4 km) to deep (189.7 km)
One tsunami alert was issued for a M5.7 event near the Kermadec Islands on Feb 8 (depth: 5.7 km)
criticisms: The report attributes the depth range 'shallow (1.4 km) to deep (189.7 km)' specifically to Nikolski, Alaska events. The 1.4 km depth belongs to '46 km E of Nikolski, Alaska' (Feb 05) which is plausibly in the Nikolski region, but the 189.7 km depth belongs to '65 km E of Aleutian Islands, Alaska' — not explicitly labeled as Nikolski. Attributing that depth to Nikolski is a stretch not clearly supported by the digest.

The daily average of '~2.7' earthquakes per day is stated as a fact. The digest shows 79 events over a 30-day window (Jan 17 – Feb 16), but the daily_counts only list 27 days with events (not all 30 days). 79/30 ≈ 2.63, which rounds to ~2.6, not ~2.7. This is a minor rounding issue but slightly inaccurate.
The report states the period is '30 days' but Jan 17 to Feb 16 inclusive is 31 days. This is a minor but verifiable inaccuracy.
The report says 'no other events in the dataset triggered a tsunami warning' — this is supported by the digest (only one tsunami=true event), so this is fine.

The report mentions 'North Maluku fault system' as context for Tobelo — this is background geological knowledge not in the digest, but it is not a factual claim derived from the digest data, so it is an added assertion that cannot be verified from the digest. It is not necessarily wrong, but it is not traceable to the source.
